newsitem.title: BELGIUM: New book on effect on Ireland of UK EU attitude.
newsitem.headline: New book on effect on Ireland of UK EU attitude.

text.p: Britain's relations with the European Union are as important to Ireland's well-being as the so-called Irish Question that dominated 19th century politics, according to a new book.

"Britain's European Question: The Issue for Ireland", published by Dublin's Institute for European Affairs (IEA), suggests the inter-dependence of Ireland and Britain needs to be sustained in a way that respects the interests of both.
"Only in this way will the twin objectives of Irish policy be attained -- peace in Northern Ireland and prosperity in Europe," the publishers said in a statement.
The book is edited by Paul Gillespie, foreign editor of The Irish Times and is based on a project set up by the IEA after the 1992-93 Irish currency crisis.
Former Irish Prime Minister Garret FitzGerald chaired the project.
The book costs 15 Irish pounds. For more information contact: Institute of European Affairs, Europe House, 8 North Great Georges Street, Dublin 1, Ireland. Tel: (353) 1 874-6756.
